title: Quayside Morning

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: The pawnbroker. Be nice about the lumbago, and help him take the morning delivery. The search is the price of the ledger.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: Gulls audition loudly for the role of witnesses. The harbor smells of tar, salt, and other people's business.

caseLine: Quayside. The pawnbroker talks after the inventory is done.

title: Item 77

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: Item 77: one brass sextant, pledged T. FINCH, forty crowns — redeemed October 12th, cash, new notes.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: Pledged broke, redeemed rich, the morning after the theft. New notes have a story, Halloway.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: The sad museum man drinks at the Anchor. {gran}'s second kitchen. We'll go at evening bell.

caseLine: Ticket 77 was Finch's. Pledged broke; redeemed rich, the morning after.

peopleFacts.fact: Debt paid off the morning after the theft.

title: The Anchor at Evening

lines.speaker: finch
lines.en: All quiet that night. Doors locked. I'd swear it on my sextant.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: He just redeemed that sextant. The lie lands as tragedy wearing a bowtie. The Chalk's board does the rest of the talking.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: In this room, debts are weather. Everyone knows the forecast.

caseLine: Finch lies kindly and badly: 'all quiet, doors locked.'

peopleFacts.fact: Lied about the night — kindly and badly.

title: The Lockbox Ledger

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: The harbor master's lockbox opens on the berth ledger: a painting-sized crate went to the SS Vesper, berth 9, dawn after the theft.

lines.speaker: holt
lines.en: Your client doubled the policy three weeks before the theft. Does Aldermere insure its own miracles, Halloway?

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: The S02 memo answers him: routine unveiling escalation, board-approved. Pettibone's telegram closes it — 'Clause 9 applies to neither of us, Inspector.'

caseLine: A painting-sized crate went to the SS Vesper at dawn. The policy jab dies on paper.

peopleFacts.fact: Tests you once, then shares the warrant. Fair.

title: Light as Gulls' Bones

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: The stevedores' verdict, unanimous and unpaid: the crate was 'light as gulls' bones.'

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: Someone wanted this trail found. Gift-wrapped, ribbon and all.

caseLine: The crate was light as gulls' bones. The trail is gift-wrapped.

title: The Half-Crack

lines.speaker: finch
lines.en: You don't understand. The papers were right. Grand old seal, proper stamps. They said insurance. They said discretion.

lines.speaker: finch
lines.en: The couriers had a password. Soft, like a bird's name. Foreign. I— I can't say it right. I never could.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: Mr. Finch. {gran} pawned her wedding spoons twice. Shame is just love with no budget.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: He is more afraid of someone than of Holt. He glances at his coat when he says he kept nothing.

caseLine: Finch let 'couriers' in — grand papers, a bird-name password. He rewrote the log.

peopleFacts.fact: Coerced with perfect paperwork; a bird-name password he can't pronounce.

title: Nine Kilograms

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: The customs stamp bears Casal's dealer mark — and the manifest declares the crate at nine kilograms. Empty from the start. Theater.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: Empty cage, empty crate. This harbor's a theater, and the theater bills Casal.

lines.speaker: holt
lines.en: Then we see the impresario. Grand Hotel, they say. Bring your good manners; he collects them.

caseLine: The crate weighed nine kilograms — empty since dawn. The stamp wears Casal's mark.

peopleFacts.fact: The forged stamp wears his mark. Somebody is very helpful about it.

flavorChoice.dry: The theater bills Casal. Let's audit the theater.
flavorChoice.warm: Someone's framing a frame-dealer. Even he deserves better.
